title: Reflection (power, cost, and when it is the wrong tool)
hook: Reflection lets you inspect and invoke types at run time from metadata — powerful for frameworks and plugins, but slow and fragile compared to compile-time code. Prefer source generators when you need metadata-driven code without run-time discovery.

blocks.text: System.Reflection APIs load assemblies, enumerate types, read attributes, and invoke methods by name. typeof(T) and Activator.CreateInstance are common entry points. Dynamic dispatch bypasses compile-time checking — typos become run-time exceptions. Trimming and Native Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation require reflection roots or they strip unused code.

entries.plainDefinition: Run-time inspection and invocation of types using assembly metadata.
Creates instances of types when you only know the Type at run time.
Linker removes unused IL; reflection targets may need preservation attributes.

blocks.text: Dependency injection containers, serializers, and ORMs use reflection heavily — you consume it more than you write it. Hand-rolled reflection in hot paths (SQS message dispatch by string name) hurts latency and breaks refactor-rename. Source generators can emit strongly typed dispatch tables at compile time instead.

blocks.title: When reflection is fine
blocks.body: One-time startup scanning — registering endpoints, building DI graphs. Not per-message hot paths.

snippet.label: Discover handlers at startup
snippet.explanation: One-time scan registers all IMessageHandler implementations. Fine at startup; not per SQS message.

snippet.label: Read custom attribute
snippet.explanation: Framework-style attribute discovery. MethodInfo and attributes come from metadata.

snippet.label: Prefer compile-time dispatch
snippet.explanation: Switch or dictionary of delegates avoids per-call GetMethod and Invoke.

blocks.title: Dynamic discovery
rows: Limited; no full type system at runtime in JS

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Reflection inside tight loops. No trim/AOT annotations when publishing Native AOT. Catching TargetInvocationException without inspecting InnerException.

interviewTakeaways: Reflection inspects metadata at run time — flexible but costly.
Fine for startup; avoid on per-request hot paths.
Source generators replace many reflection patterns with compile-time code.
commonPitfalls: GetMethod with wrong binding flags — null at runtime.
Native AOT trims reflected types without roots.

jsTsCorrelations.note: import() loads modules dynamically. C# reflection loads types from already-loaded assemblies — different mechanism, similar plugin patterns.
